sentences.text: Heard learned counsel appearing for the Date: 2025.10.13 parties.
2. Perused the records.

3. FIR No.79/2016 was registered at Police Station Namkum, District Ranchi, Jharkhand for the offence punishable under sections 406 & 420 of the Indian Penal Code, against the petitioner and co-accused on the ground that they had duped the complainant by inducing him and his wife to mortgage the house i.e., immovable property standing in the name of complainants wife and obtained a loan, misused the blank cheques, misappropriate the funds borrowed in the name of complainants wife and out of the amount so received, the accused had purchased another immovable property and has not repaid the amount. Whereas the petitioner has asserted that it is a private loan and he has been regularly paying interest.
It is an undisputed fact that accused no.1- Mukesh Kumar Ram has been granted anticipatory bail by the jurisdictional High Court.
In fact, in the anticipatory bail application no.2620/2025 filed by the petitioner, it was conceded by the State that the custodial interrogation was no longer necessary.

4. In that view of the matter, we are of the considered view that petitioner would be entitled to be released on anticipatory bail, particularly in the backdrop of charge sheet also having been filed.

5. Petitioner is directed to be released on anticipatory bail subject to the further conditions that petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional Court on all dates of hearing without fail and even a single day of his absence would result in automatic cancellation of this order of granting anticipatory bail unless exempted by the jurisdictional Court for any cogent reason.
Consequently the prayer of the petitioner is allowed.
6. With these observations, the present petition is disposed of.

7. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
(NIRMALA NEGI) (AVGV RAMU)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS COURT MASTER (NSH)
